heading: Appendix C Symbols and notation
introduction: This glossary covers the mathematical notation used in the text and numbered equations. Definitions are local to each study; identical letters can denote different quantities. Equation numbers refer to the combined manuscript. Numerical model settings and units remain specified in the methods.
rows: i, j; n
Participant indices; n is the number of participants in the relevant training or evaluation set, not the number of EEG segments.
X, x, Xᵢ, xᵢ
X denotes basic information before acquisition; x is a particular value and Xᵢ the information for participant i. In the logistic-model paragraph, xᵢ denotes the inputs to that classifier.
Z
Advanced measurements available after acquisition, such as a biomarker panel or EEG features. Study A, equations (1) and (4).
Y, yᵢ
Binary recorded outcome and the observed outcome of participant i. Positive means CDR > 0 in OASIS and AD in the other tasks; it is not uniformly biomarker-confirmed AD.
p₀, p_b,i, pᵢᴮ
Basic-model probability of the positive class. The three forms are the notation used respectively in Studies A, B and C.
p₁, p_a,i, pᵢᴬ
Advanced-model probability using the additional measurements. The forms correspond to Studies A, B and C.
G(x), Gᵢ
Expected reduction in Brier loss from acquiring advanced information, conditional on basic information; Gᵢ is the benefit for candidate i. Equation (1).
Ĝᵢ, ε
Estimated benefit and a hypothetical uniform bound on its absolute estimation error. The paper does not estimate or certify ε empirically. Equation (3).
S, |S|; k
Selected set, its number of members, and the fixed number of acquisitions. In equations (2)–(3), |S| = k.
S*, Ŝ
Selection maximizing true benefit and selection maximizing estimated benefit, respectively. The hat marks estimation. Equation (3).
R(S)
Total conditional expected Brier loss for selection S. Dividing by n gives average loss; equation (3) bounds excess total loss.
η₀, η₁; G Bayes(x)
Coherent Bayes probabilities E[Y|X] and E[Y|X,Z], and their conditional Brier improvement. Under these assumptions, the improvement is Var(η₁|X=x). Equation (4).
gᵢ
Realized cross-fitted Brier improvement used as a gate-training target. Study B uses the blended advanced probability; Study C equation (10) uses pᵢᴬ.
q; floor(qn)
In Study A and the capacity analysis, q is the nominal acquisition fraction. floor(qn) is the integer number of acquired panels in a batch of n participants.
rᵢ, pᵢᴿ; m
Binary referral indicator, routed probability, and evaluation-batch size in Study C. Equation (11) acquires floor(0.3m) panels. This scalar m differs from the posterior vector m in equation (5).
In the hypothetical cost analysis, w is false-negative cost relative to false-positive cost, c is acquisition cost in those same units, and 1/(1+w) is the corresponding decision threshold.
H(p)
Bernoulli entropy −p log(p) − (1−p) log(1−p). The Gaussian information comparator uses H(mean p₁) − mean H(p₁) across its conditional draws.

heading: Symbols for fitting and representation
introduction: These symbols describe the fitted acquisition gates, probability blend, EEG representation and classifiers. Posterior uncertainty, signal covariance and sample variability are different quantities.
rows: φ(x)
Design vector for the Bayesian linear benefit gate: standardized basic inputs together with an explicit constant. Equation (5).
β, eᵢ
In the Bayesian gate, β is the coefficient vector and eᵢ is Gaussian residual noise in gᵢ = φ(Xᵢ)ᵀβ + eᵢ.
m, Σ
Posterior mean vector and posterior covariance matrix of the Bayesian gate coefficients, conditional on fitted upstream models. Equation (5). Σ here is a matrix, not a summation sign.
μ(x), s(x)
Posterior mean benefit and posterior standard deviation of the conditional mean benefit. s(x) excludes observation noise and upstream fitting uncertainty. Equation (5).
κ, aκ(x)
Nonnegative uncertainty-penalty multiplier and adjusted referral score μ(x) − κs(x). Primary comparison: κ = 1 versus 0. Equation (5).
dᵢ
Difference between advanced and basic cross-fitted probabilities, p_a,i − p_b,i. Equations (6)–(7).
α, α*
Blend coefficient in [0,1] and its training-fitted minimizer. α = 0 gives basic prediction; α = 1 gives advanced prediction. α is not a significance level here.
qᵢ(α)
Blended probability p_b,i + αdᵢ. This function differs from the acquisition fraction q and the Wilson observed proportion q.
L(α)
Mean squared probability error on the cross-fitted training pairs as a function of α. Equation (6); its constrained minimizer is equation (7).
Cᴼᴬˢ
EEG covariance matrix estimated by Oracle Approximating Shrinkage. This is a signal covariance matrix, distinct from the gate posterior covariance Σ. Equation (8).
C̃, tr(Cᴼᴬˢ)
Trace-normalized EEG covariance and the trace (sum of diagonal entries) of its unnormalized estimate. Equation (8).
log(C̃)
Matrix logarithm of the normalized covariance, formed through its eigenvalues and eigenvectors after the stated eigenvalue floor. It is not an element-by-element logarithm.
vecₛᵧₘ, z
Upper-triangle vectorization of the symmetric matrix logarithm, with off-diagonal entries weighted by √2, and the resulting feature vector. Equation (8).
C
Inverse regularization strength for logistic regression or SVC in the model descriptions. Larger C permits less shrinkage. It is distinct from the covariance matrix Cᴼᴬˢ.
β₀, β; ηᵢ
Logistic intercept, coefficient vector and linear score ηᵢ = β₀ + βᵀxᵢ. This ηᵢ is a logit, whereas η₀ and η₁ in equation (4) are Bayes probabilities.
σ(u), exp(u)
Logistic sigmoid σ(u) = 1/(1 + exp(−u)) and the exponential function. u is a generic real-valued argument.
t, T, t*
Decision threshold, finite candidate-threshold set, and largest feasible source-selected threshold at or below 0.5 attaining the fitting sensitivity target. Equation (9).
pᵢ, pⱼ
Positive-class probabilities for participants i and j under the model being evaluated; in threshold fitting they are cross-fitted training probabilities. Equations (9), (13) and (14).

heading: Symbols for evaluation and mathematical operators
introduction: The definitions below separate observed counts from fitted probabilities and make the interval calculations explicit. Repeated-validation means are descriptive averages, not fractions of individual participants.
rows: TP, FN
True positives: positive-class participants correctly detected. False negatives: positive-class participants missed at the stated threshold. In the external study the positive class is AD.
TN, FP

True negatives: comparator participants correctly classified. False positives: comparator participants incorrectly classified as positive. The external comparator is healthy control; the original EEG comparator is FTD.
Sensitivity, specificity
TP/(TP+FN) and TN/(TN+FP), respectively. Their denominators are 12 AD cases and 11 controls in the external study. Equation (12).
Brier
Average squared difference between predicted probability and observed binary outcome. Lower values indicate better probability accuracy on the evaluated sample. Equation (13).
AUROC; n₁, n₀
Area under the receiver operating characteristic curve; positive- and negative-class sample sizes. Equation (14) counts positive-negative score orderings and gives ties half credit.
k, n, q in Wilson intervals
Number of successes, relevant binomial denominator and observed proportion q = k/n. For sensitivity, k = TP and n = TP+FN; for specificity, k = TN and n = TN+FP.
z in Wilson intervals
Standard-normal critical value 1.96 for the stated two-sided 95% interval. This scalar z differs from the EEG feature vector z in equation (8).
c, h in Wilson intervals
Interval centre and half-width, giving c ± h. Equations (15)–(16). This c is not the acquisition cost used in Study A.
Expectation, variance, and conditioning on the information after the vertical bar; for example E[Y|X].
Σᵢ, Σⱼ
Summation over the indicated indices. A restriction such as i:yᵢ=1 selects positive-class participants; i∈S selects members of S.
1[condition]
Indicator equal to 1 when the bracketed condition is true and 0 otherwise. Used for threshold decisions and pairwise score comparisons.
clip(v,0,1), floor(v)
Projection of v onto [0,1], and the greatest integer no larger than v, respectively. They constrain blend weights and round acquisition counts down.
Superscript T; hat; *
T on a vector denotes transpose. A hat denotes an estimate. A star denotes the specified optimizer or selected optimum, not statistical significance.
Absolute value for a scalar v, cardinality for a set S, square root, and plus-or-minus. Their meaning depends on the enclosed object.
Set membership, less-than-or-equal and greater-than-or-equal. Exponents −1 and 2 denote a reciprocal/inverse and a square, respectively, according to the object.
AD, FTD, HC, MCI, CDR
Alzheimer disease; frontotemporal dementia; healthy control; mild cognitive impairment; Clinical Dementia Rating. Endpoints and comparator diagnoses remain study-specific.
EEG, MMSE, CSF, PCA, OAS
Electroencephalography; Mini-Mental State Examination; cerebrospinal fluid; principal component analysis; Oracle Approximating Shrinkage. Here OAS is an estimator, not an OASIS cohort.
eTIV, nWBV; Hz, SD, CI
Estimated total intracranial volume; normalized whole-brain volume; hertz (cycles per second); standard deviation; confidence interval. Hypothetical cost units are separately defined in Study A.
